name: Colvor Announcement Bar
author: colvor

sections.description:
Colvor Announcement Bar is local-first. Install it, open Settings > Announcement Bar, create your message, and save. Free use requires no Colvor account, connection, token, heartbeat, or configuration synchronization.

The front end reads only the colvor_announcement_config WordPress option. It never contacts Colvor, so an existing bar keeps rendering if Colvor is unavailable.

Free includes:

  • Enable or disable the bar.
  • Announcement text.
  • Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, and inline text color.
  • Background color.
  • Selected-text size in the editor, with a rem slider and custom px, rem, em, vw, vh, vmin, vmax, or % units.

Pro adds:

  • Link and link underline control.
  • All-page or selected-path scope.
  • Scroll speed, including a static mode.
  • Letter and item spacing with rem sliders or custom units, plus a separator.

Setup

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Settings > Announcement Bar.
  3. Create the bar and save it.
  4. Optionally purchase Pro, paste a License Key or Promotion Code, and click Activate.

External services

Free configuration and visitor page loads do not use an external service.

Colvor at https://colvor.com is contacted only when an administrator explicitly clicks Upgrade to Pro, Activate, or Deactivate. Activate sends the entered License Key or Promotion Code, a random plugin installation identifier, and the plugin version to /api/v1/license/activate. Deactivate sends the activation identifier and random installation identifier to /api/v1/license/deactivate. The plugin does not send visitor activity, page content, users, posts, WooCommerce orders, or payment details.

If an activation or deactivation request fails, the existing local configuration and last valid Pro state are kept. An expired License locks Pro editing but does not remove or alter the current bar.

See the Colvor Privacy Policy.
sections.faq:
Does Free require an account or connection?

No. Free works entirely inside WordPress immediately after activation.

Does the front end validate my License?

No. License operations occur only in WordPress admin after an explicit administrator action. Visitor pages render from local data.

What happens when Pro expires?

Pro controls become read-only. The existing announcement and styling continue to render from the saved local configuration.
sections.changelog:
0.5.2

  • Update license input placeholder to a generic prompt supporting both license keys and promotion codes.
  • Preserve strikethrough formatting through saving and ensure reliable front-end display.
  • Move announcement bar toggle above the text editor for streamlined setup.

0.5.1

  • Keep the bar visible near the top on themes without the wp_body_open hook.
  • Measure the scrolling cycle in the front end and keep zero speed static.
  • Treat an emptied rich-text editor as blank so no empty bar appears.
  • Preserve spaces between words when adjacent text has different rich-text formatting.
  • Keep selected inline text colors after saving in WordPress.
  • Organize the WordPress settings page around the announcement editor, with grouped Pro controls and a separate License section.
  • Let Free users adjust only selected text size in the editor with a rem slider or custom units.
  • Add matching rem sliders and custom unit inputs for Pro letter and item spacing while preserving older px settings.
  • Close the background color picker by clicking outside it, using WordPress’s built-in picker.

0.5.0

  • Move the complete Announcement Bar editor into WordPress.
  • Remove Announcement Bar dependency on Connect, Guest Workspace, Site Token, heartbeat, and cloud configuration sync.
  • Add local License Key and Promotion Code activation with one-installation entitlement.
  • Keep visitor rendering completely local and preserve existing configuration during License API failures or expiry.

0.4.9

  • Store and render the current announcement from colvor_announcement_config.
